OFFICE OF ACQUISITION MANAGEMENT

ICE Acquisition Manual 3006.301-90

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 41 USC 3304 (A): USE OF NONCOMPETITIVE PROCEDURES J&A-26-0233

Pursuant to the requirements of the Competition in Contracting Act (CICA) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103 (FAR Class Deviation 25-11.1) and in accordance with the requirements of RFO 6.104, the justification for the use of the statutory authority under RFO 6.103 is justified by the following facts and rationale required under RFO 6.104-1 as follows:

1. Agency and Contracting Activity. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Office of Acquisition Management (OAQ), proposes to extend an existing hybrid contract with both firm-fixed price (FFP) and cost reimbursable (CR) contract line-item numbers (CLINs) on behalf of the Enforcement, Removals, and Operations Division (ERO) on a basis of other than full and open competition.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved. (a) Nature of action: OAQ procured, on a sole source basis, comprehensive Operational Support Aircraft Maintenance (OSAM) based on ERO’s Statement of Objectives (SOO). DHS has an urgent need for the continuation of a performance-based, multi-mission OSAM contract utilizing Government Furnished Aircraft (GFA) under a Government-Owned, ContractorOperated (GOCO) construct. The contractor shall continue to maintain one C-37B Gulfstream 650ER GFA to support and maintain airworthiness. The contractor shall provide maintenance and minimal operational support for inter-agency aircraft use agreement missions upon receipt of written authorization from DHS and confirmation of funding arrangements from the requesting agency. The Government requires the contractor to deliver and maintain a safe, compliant, mission-ready aviation enterprise that operates with transparency, discipline, and enterprise-level governance.

This requirement will continue providing the personnel, engineering services, and supply chain management necessary to ensure continuous airworthiness of the aircraft. The contractor will support comprehensive scheduled and unscheduled maintenance in alignment with OEM guidance, airworthiness directives, and other FAA regulatory requirements. At the time of award, the contractor is expected to operate and maintain a government furnished C-37B Gulfstream 650ER aircraft.

The one-month extension will have a period of performance of July 30, 2026, through August 27, 2026. DHS originally utilized this aircraft through charter flights procured under a DHS IDIQ; however, once the aircraft was purchased by DHS and became GFA, the operations and maintenance of the aircraft was not addressed through contract support. DHS awarded a six-week sole source contract for O&M upon taking ownership of the aircraft. The contract ended May 12, 2026. All citations in this document follow applicable DHS RFO Deviations therefore are referred as RFO.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a one-month option period from May 28, 2026 through July 27, 2026 as the contracting office worked toward a longer-term contract to support both operations and maintenance. The longer-term contract encountered an unexpected delay and maintenance on one of the G650ERs is still required. For this reason, we are extending the contract for the required maintenance of one G650ER. Aircraft become non-air-airworthy in short order and can endure significant damage if they are not regularly maintained and utilized, to include flight operations. While the aircraft is owned/possessed by the Government, the proposed sole source vendor below has been maintaining this aircraft for the last few months.

The urgency surrounding the sole source award for aircraft maintenance was driven by several unusual and compelling factors. Aircraft require continuous, specialized maintenance and operational activity to remain airworthy; even brief lapses can lead to rapid degradation, costly repairs, or permanent loss of certification. As maintenance contract 70CDCR26P00000010 expired before the new operations and maintenance contract could be awarded, it is critical that we extend it through mutual agreement of the parties to ensure the proper maintenance is completed on the G650ER to avoid jeopardizing the aircraft’s condition and value.

The incumbent Contractor possesses unique, immediate access to the aircraft as it is already housed and maintained at their facility pursuant to the current contract. No other vendor could mobilize the necessary resources, personnel, and equipment on such short notice without risking the aircraft’s airworthiness. Furthermore, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) regulations mandate strict adherence to maintenance schedules and operational checks; failure to comply could result in regulatory penalties, loss of airworthiness certificates, and inability to deploy the aircraft for mission-critical operations. This aircraft is essential for DHS mission requirements, and any period of non-availability directly impacts operational readiness, homeland security, and public safety.

There are no viable alternatives at this time as no other vendor can provide the required maintenance and operational support within the necessary timeframe. The urgency is compounded by the risk that attempting to compete the requirement or transition to another vendor would introduce delays, during which the aircraft would be unmaintained and at risk. While OAQ has worked diligently to award a one-year O&M contract ████████████████████████ various circumstances have left that award still pending. The Government is acting promptly to mitigate risk and ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards, and the extension of this contract is a temporary measure to bridge the gap until the longer-term solution can be put in place.

(h) Background information about the requirement: This is an extension of a sole source requirement for aircraft maintenance procured by ICE DCR in May 2026.

3. Description of Supplies/Services. This is an immediate and continuing requirement for routine and non-routine maintenance support, aircraft readiness activities, maintenance coordination, discrepancy resolution, inspection support, and limited flight activity necessary to validate maintenance actions or aircraft systems performance. Key activities supported through this contract include the following items:

1) Maintenance, Engineering, and Airworthiness Support: The contractor will ensure the aircraft maintains continuous airworthiness, high operational readiness, and optimized lifecycle sustainment, while minimizing mission disruption through proactive maintenance planning and responsive technical support.

The current maintenance forecast shows schedule tasks coming due each month from August through December. ICE has elected to complete all of the known maintenance tasks through the end of the year during the August maintenance visit thereby saving approximately $100,000 and avoiding an additional 17 days of aircraft downtime that Page - 3 - of 11

This also allows the completion of the December Flight Data Recorder inspection in which the unit has to be removed and sent to Gulfstream which allows for that 10-day process to occur during existing downtime. This also resets and annualizes the aircraft’s calendar-based maintenance going forward.

2) Management, Staffing, and Operation of Aircraft: Maintenance activities shall be conducted in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, aircraft technical data, manufacturer guidance, maintenance program requirements, Government direction, and aircraft-specific readiness priorities. The contractor shall provide the personnel, management oversight, procedures, coordination mechanisms, and technical support necessary to safely and effectively maintain the aircraft in an appropriate readiness posture throughout the period of performance. To meet this requirement, the contractor shall perform the following: a. Provide qualified pilots to support maintenance-related flights, functional check flights, test flights, repositioning flights, post-maintenance validation flights, and other limited flight activities required to maintain or validate aircraft readiness b. Provide qualified maintenance personnel and technical subject matter experts to coordinate, support, and implement scheduled and unscheduled maintenance activities for the G650ER aircraft. c. Conduct maintenance coordination, discrepancy tracking, inspection support, servicing support, return-to-service planning, and readiness validation activities in accordance with applicable aircraft technical data, maintenance requirements, and Government direction. d. Provide program management personnel to coordinate maintenance priorities, track mission-critical milestones, support Government reporting requirements, and ensure timely execution of OSAM activities during the period of performance. e. Coordination between the Government, aircraft maintenance providers, OEM representatives, avionics providers, secure communications stakeholders, and other authorized parties, as required, to support aircraft readiness and completion of required maintenance or accreditation-related activities.

3) Safety, Compliance, and Airworthiness: GFA will be maintained in accordance with applicable DHS-specific Flight Program Standards. When performing test, maintenance, Government personnel transportation, or other domestic activities, such operations will be conducted as Public Aircraft Operations (PAO) pursuant to 49 U.S.C. §§ 40102(a)(41) and 40125. For missions conducted under these designations, aircraft will be maintained in accordance with Part 91 before and after each operation. Flight safety standards will conform to DHS Flight Program Standards. 4) Reporting, Data Management, and Operational Transparency The contractor shall provide transparent, accurate, and timely reporting in accordance with mutually agreed-upon contract deliverables to ensure continuous Government situational awareness, effective oversight, and informed decision-making.

4. Identification of statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition. This justification is prepared pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2), implemented by RFO 6.1032, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, which permits contracting without providing for full and open competition when the Government’s need for supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured, financially or otherwise, unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits proposals.

The 150-day period of performance limitation at HSAR 3006.103-2(c)(70)) (HSAR Class Deviation 25-01) applies to this procurement.

The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. §3304 as implemented by:

6. Demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited. (a) Rationale for using the authority cited in section 4 of the J&A. The authority that applies to this justification is RFO 6.103-2: Unusual and compelling urgency due to the continued need for maintenance on this Government Owned Aircraft. Without sufficient maintenance, the aircraft will quickly fall into disrepair, become non airworthy, and will significantly impact the operational mission of ERO. The planned one-month extension allows sufficient time to finish working toward a more permanent solution in accordance with RFO 6.103-2(d).

The unusual and compelling urgency in this case is from the U.S. President’s declaration of a national emergency to remove dangerous illegal aliens who have entered the U.S. without proper legal authority. Although the national emergency declared by the U.S. President regarding the removal of dangerous illegal aliens has been in effect for over a year, operational demands and risks to homeland security have continued to escalate. A previous six-week sole source contract was awarded by DHS immediately after the purchase of these aircraft to allow time for a competitive solicitation; however, the extensive DHS shutdown prohibited that action. The 2-month maintenance contract expired while a new operations and maintenance contract is being negotiated; since that requirement has not been awarded yet, it is imperative that we extend it one month through mutual agreement of the parties to ensure the G650ER remains airworthy and receives the required maintenance.

The connection between the emergency and the urgent need for this maintenance contract remains direct and critical. Without immediate award, there is a substantial risk of fleet degradation, which would compromise the Department’s ability to respond to national security threats and fulfill removal operations. Adding further delay to facilitate a full competitive process would likely result in irreparable harm to operational readiness and asset integrity, outweighing the benefits of competition under these unique circumstances.

(b) Details covering what events lead to the situation requiring use of other than full and open competition procedures including whether any portion of the work can be segregated to allow for competition. Recent circumstances have prevented the government from pursuing full and open competition for this requirement. The short-term Maintenance (OSAM) contract expired before a new operations and maintenance contract could be awarded due to unforeseen delays in the DHS procurement process. To mitigate this delay, OAQ is extending it an additional month through mutual agreement of the parties to ensure there is no loss of required regular maintenance coverage for the aircraft to remain airworthy, receive engine lubrication, and undergo periodic system checks. Without a maintenance contract in place, these essential tasks cannot be performed, risking degradation of the aircraft and loss of operational capability.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement The nature of the required maintenance is such that it cannot be segregated or deferred; the aircraft must be serviced in accordance with regulations to ensure mission readiness. No portion of the work can be separated for competition without compromising the integrity of the maintenance program and operational requirements.

(c) Summarize alternatives considered and why they will not work; and Under the current circumstances, several alternatives to the proposed sole-source action were evaluated, including conducting a full and open competition and pursuing a limited competition among multiple vendors; however, both alternatives were determined to be unworkable due to the urgency of the requirement.

A full and open competition would require significant lead time for market research, solicitation development, proposal submission, evaluation, and award. Based on recent procurement timelines for similar requirements, this process would take more time than is available. This delay would limit support for ERO and other Agency and Governmental support missions due to a lapse of critical maintenance, resulting in operational disruptions, increased risk to mission continuity, and potential impacts to public safety and security. A limited competition among pre-qualified vendors was also considered. While this approach could reduce the procurement timeline somewhat, it would still require time for vendor identification, proposal solicitation, and evaluation. Even with expedited procedures, the anticipated delays would be incompatible with the immediate need for uninterrupted maintenance support.

The urgency of the requirement stems from the fact that ERO and other Agency missions rely on continuous, comprehensive maintenance support to sustain essential operations. Any gap in support would jeopardize the Agency’s ability to fulfill its statutory obligations, respond to emergent situations, and maintain operational readiness. Delays caused by competitive procurement processes would directly impact mission-critical functions, including facility management, equipment reliability, and the ability to support law enforcement and public safety operations.

Given these considerations, the sole-source action is justified as the only viable approach to ensure immediate and uninterrupted maintenance support for ERO and other Agency and Governmental missions. The risks associated with procurement delays outweigh the benefits of competition in this instance.

(d) Impact to the mission that would result if the J&A is not approved and, consequently, the product or service is not provided. Under these circumstances, failure to approve this J&A would adversely impact DHS’s ability to maintain the C-37B Gulfstream owned by the Government. There would be additional cost to get the aircraft back to operational readiness. If the required maintenance for the DHS-owned C-37B Gulfstream 650ER aircraft is not completed, the plane will quickly become non-airworthy, with critical systems such as engines, hydraulics, avionics, and environmental controls degrading due to inactivity. For example, engines require regular operation for proper oil lubrication; if left idle for more Page - 7 - of 11

As inspections lapse and airworthiness directives are not met, the aircraft will violate regulatory requirements and may suffer physical damage, including discharged batteries, flat-spotted tires, and dried seals.

Currently, the designated DHS/ICE AIR aircraft required for these operations is due for 111 scheduled maintenance tasks in August to satisfy mandatory maintenance inspections and component replacements. Without immediate contracted maintenance support, the aircraft will be grounded.

The maintenance contract’s short period of performance is specifically designed to bridge the gap while a longer-term operations contract is finalized, ensuring continuous support for these critical missions.

Any delay in awarding this contract would result in immediate operational downtime, non-compliance with federal aviation safety requirements, and the inability to fulfill urgent border security objectives. The risk is not hypothetical; it is tied to ongoing and anticipated operations that require uninterrupted aircraft availability.

If these planes remain non-airworthy for long, the government could incur costs related to engine preservation/auxiliary power unit (APU) work at $41,000.00 per month, crew retraining at $10,000.00 per month, and required inspections/compliance at an additional $41,000.00 per month.

Salus Worldwide Solutions Corp is uniquely positioned to provide immediate mobilization and maintenance services within the required timeframe, ensuring the aircraft remain safe, reliable, and available for these urgent operations. Full and open competition would introduce unacceptable delays and jeopardize the government’s ability to respond to current and emerging border security threats.

7. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable. The proposed contract action was not publicized in accordance with RFO 5.101(b)(2) whereas this contract action is unusual and compelling urgency and precludes competition to the maximum extent practicable, and the Government would be seriously injured if the agency complies with the time periods specified pursuant in RFO 5.101. Efforts to solicit offers from multiple sources were limited due to the unique circumstances surrounding this requirement. Prior to the current urgent need, the Government assessed the market and determined that only a limited number of sources were capable of providing the required maintenance support. Given the immediate life-safety and mission-critical timelines, further solicitation at this stage would result in unacceptable delays. Therefore, the Government proceeded without broader competition to ensure continuity of operations and to meet the compelling and urgent need for maintenance support. Consistent with the requirements of the cited authority, The Government will, to the maximum extent practicable, seek to expand consideration of additional responsible sources for any follow-on or longer-term requirements once the immediate emergency has stabilized. ICE DCR is in the process of awarding a one-year Operations and Maintenance contract for this aircraft and others in the ICE fleet. This process will support subsequent phases of the effort or establish a more enduring contract mechanism.

This justification will be posted in accordance with RFO 6.301.

8. Determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The contracting officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The proposed contract structure utilizes firm-fixed-price CLINs for maintenance oversight, maintenance flight hours, and fixed ownership amounts, combined with cost reimbursement of actual incurred other direct costs (exclusive of profit), which aligns contractor compensation with verifiable costs and defined performance outputs.

This month long extension is at the same fair and reasonable rates already determined ensuring a fair and reasonable price going forward.

9. Description of Market Research. From July 8, 2026 — July 22, 2026, market research was conducted by DCR through the issuance of a Request for Information (RFI) posted on SAM.gov in support of a future competitive procurement for Aircraft O&M support. Approximately 16 vendors reached out in response to the RFI to express their interest in a future competitive solicitation.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement During the original sole source procurement, the Government faced urgent operational requirements that precluded the possibility of conducting a full and open competition. The accelerated timeline continues to be driven by mission-critical needs, and there is insufficient time to issue a competitive solicitation, allow for proposal development, and complete the evaluation process. As a result, extending the PoP of this sole source contract is necessary to ensure continuity of services and prevent mission disruption. These timing constraints remain relevant, as the process to conduct a competitive procurement would not allow the Government to meet its immediate needs. Since there is an immediate need for maintenance support, it was determined that the best plan of action is to extend this current contract to provide the time necessary to put a more permanent O&M solution in place. Due to the urgent, life- and timesensitive nature of the requirement, formal, comprehensive market research sufficient to support full and open competition could not be completed without jeopardizing mission timelines and increasing risk to personnel in life threatening environments. Salus Worldwide Solutions Corp. has spent the last 60 days providing this support and has demonstrated the necessary combination of established operational readiness infrastructure and demonstrated aircraft operations experience to continue supporting this requirement.

10. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition. None. All relevant facts have already been discussed.

11. A listing of the sources, if any that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition. No sources expressed written interest in this short-term acquisition.

12. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for supplies or services required. Before any subsequent acquisition for these supplies or services, the agency will take steps to remove or overcome barriers to competition. This will include expanding the market research conducted to identify additional potential sources, engaging with industry to clarify requirements, and revising technical specifications or statements of work to eliminate unnecessary restrictions. The agency will also publicize future requirements to maximize vendor awareness and participation and assess any proprietary or sole-source constraints to determine if they can be removed. These actions are intended to foster greater competition and ensure compliance with Federal Acquisition Regulation requirements for full and open competition in future acquisitions.
